question: In the DX-Scorecard MBR builder, per-KPI "delta vs last MBR" is defined as this month's value minus the same KPI's value in the previous published MBR, but KPI values are free-text MetricValue strings (e.g. "5.46 days", "18", "<= 1 day", "42%") or cohort SubReading[]; what algorithm parses these strings into comparable numbers, how are units/suffixes/inequalities handled, and how is the delta rendered when a value is non-numeric or unparseable?
recommendation: Add a single pure helper (e.g. `parseMetricValue(raw): { n: number, unit: string } | null`) that: (1) strips leading inequality/qualifier tokens (`<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `~`, `approx`), (2) matches the FIRST signed decimal number via regex `-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?` (removing thousands commas), and (3) captures the trailing unit/suffix by normalizing the remainder (`%`, `days`/`day`, `s`, `/day`, etc.). Compute the delta ONLY when both the current and previous readings parse to a number AND share the same normalized unit; otherwise treat it as incomparable. For cohort `SubReading[]`, parse and diff per matching `label`, never across the whole array. Render an incomparable/unparseable/unit-mismatched delta as a neutral em-dash placeholder (`—`) with no arrow or sign, so free-text values like `WIP`, `Monitor`, or `<= 1 day` never produce a misleading numeric delta.
supporting_points: The real MetricValue corpus (from docs/mocks/data.js) is heterogeneous: pure scalars ("18", "5"), percentages ("88.46%"), durations ("5.46 days", "630.39s"), rate suffixes ("434/day", "11/day (1 repo)"), inequality targets ("<= 1 day", "<= 1%"), and non-numeric statuses ("WIP") — so a first-number-plus-normalized-unit regex is the only robust approach, and comparing across mismatched units (days vs % vs /day) must be blocked to avoid nonsense deltas.

MetricValue is `string | SubReading[]` (shared/types.ts), and cohort labels (gh/gh, Moda, Copilot, Go SDLC) can be added/removed/renamed between months, so deltas must be aligned by SubReading.label with unmatched labels rendered as 'new'/'—' rather than positionally subtracted; a whole-array numeric delta is undefined.

This is currently unbuilt backlog work (BACKLOG.md M7 'Sparklines / trend arrows: compute per-metric deltas across snapshots'), so the parser should live as an isolated, unit-tested pure function that returns `null` on failure, letting the renderer fall back to a neutral non-numeric placeholder and keeping the existing Scorecard table/value contract untouched.
